summary: IMS Health Holdings Inc. operates as a global information and technology services company dedicated to measuring and improving performance within the healthcare industry by standardizing, organizing, and integrating vast datasets including sales, prescription, promotional, claims, electronic medical records, and social media data through proprietary analytics and technology infrastructure. The firm offers a comprehensive suite of products and services ranging from local information services and national and sub-national data to hosted and cloud-based applications, implementation services, subscription software, analytic services, and consulting. These offerings are engineered to support critical decision-making areas such as research and development, drug pricing, market access, commercial operations, and clinical trial management. The company serves a diverse clientele comprising pharmaceutical and biotechnology manufacturers, distributors, healthcare providers, payers, government agencies, policymakers, researchers, and the financial community. Its principal offerings include national and sub-national information products that measure pharmaceutical sales, prescribing trends, and promotional activity across retail, hospital, and mail-order channels, alongside OneKey, a reference database tracking healthcare professionals, and technology solutions for CRM, performance management, and incentive compensation. Furthermore, the company provides Real-World Evidence solutions utilizing anonymous patient-level data to analyze treatment outcomes and costs, complemented by workflow analytics and consulting services to optimize commercial operations. Serving over 5,000 clients in more than 100 countries, IMS Health delivers insights through subscription contracts, licensed services, and project-based engagements while operating a global information technology infrastructure that processes over 55 billion healthcare transactions annually. The company's primary customers are life sciences sector entities, which collectively account for approximately 90% of revenue, with additional clients including payers, government and regulatory agencies, healthcare providers, distributors, and pharmacies.

AK Steel Holding Corporation operates as a fully-integrated producer of flat-rolled carbon, stainless, and electrical steels, along with tubular products, primarily through its wholly-owned subsidiary, AK Steel Corporation. The company manufactures premium-quality coated, cold-rolled, hot-rolled, and specialty steels sold in hot band, sheet, and strip forms, while AK Tube LLC finishes flat-rolled steel into welded steel tubing specifically for the automotive, truck, and construction markets. Additionally, the firm engages in European trading activities for steel and related materials, and in 2015, it expanded its operations to include the production of metallurgical coal and trading companies in Mexico and Europe. Its primary customers include automotive manufacturers, infrastructure and manufacturing firms such as transformer and appliance makers, distributors, service centers, and converters. The company directs its marketing efforts toward customers requiring high-quality steel with precise delivery and technical support, serving diverse markets domestically and internationally. While the firm intentionally limits participation in commodity markets, it focuses on delivering high-quality products with technical support to major customers. In 2015, Ford Motor Company and Fiat Chrysler Automobiles accounted for 12% and 11% of net sales, respectively. The company serves a diverse geographic customer base primarily located within the United States, selling stainless steel to food handling, chemical processing, and medical equipment manufacturers, and electrical steel to transformer, motor, and generator makers, alongside its core sheet and strip sales to automotive manufacturers and their suppliers in the infrastructure and manufacturing sectors.

KB Home operates as a national homebuilding and financial services business serving homebuyers across the United States, with its geographic footprint expanding from four segments in 2010 to nine states by 2015 and eight states in 2020. The company constructs and sells attached and detached single-family homes, townhomes, and condominiums in development communities, urban in-fill locations, and mixed-use projects, primarily targeting first-time, move-up, and active adult homebuyers. Its core strategy involves a "Built to Order" approach where in-house sales teams work directly with customers to design custom homes, offering standard designs alongside premium options like KB Home Studios that feature energy and water efficiency. While financial services including title, insurance, and mortgage banking through a joint venture are offered, homebuilding consistently represents the vast majority of revenue, accounting for 99.6% of total revenues in both 2015 and 2020. The business model relies on acquiring land, developing communities with products ranging from smaller, higher-density units to larger premium locations, and delivering completed homes equipped with smart home automation and solar panels. Customer engagement occurs through various media channels where buyers are presented with design choices, model home previews, and financing options to facilitate homeownership. Performance is influenced by construction capacity, material costs, and housing market activity, characterized by seasonal sales patterns that traditionally peak in spring and early summer, with first-time and first-move-up buyers constituting approximately 78% of annual deliveries.

Linde PLC operates as the world's largest industrial gas company, primarily selling atmospheric gases such as oxygen, nitrogen, argon, and rare gases, alongside process gases including carbon dioxide, helium, hydrogen, electronic gases, specialty gases, and acetylene. The firm also designs and constructs equipment for gas production, providing services for olefin, natural gas, air separation, hydrogen, and synthesis gas plants. Distribution methods encompass on-site tonnage, merchant bulk liquid, and packaged cylinder gases. This diverse portfolio serves a wide array of industries, including healthcare, petroleum refining, manufacturing, food and beverage, fiber-optics, steel making, aerospace, chemicals, electronics, and water treatment. Operating on a global scale, the company maintains a presence in Europe, Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and North America, with approximately 69% of its sales generated outside the United States.

American Water Works Company operates as a water and wastewater utility provider serving approximately 15 million people across over 30 U.S. states and two Canadian provinces through regulated businesses and market-based operations. The Regulated Businesses segment owns and operates utilities for residential, commercial, industrial, and public authority customers, delivering drinking water, wastewater services, and sale-for-resale water through an extensive network of transmission and distribution infrastructure. Billing is based on consumption and base fees or fixed charges. The company grows its regulated footprint by acquiring small utility systems and selling water to other community water systems. The Market-Based Operations segment provides contract-based services including facility operation and maintenance for the military and industry, pipe repair and leak protection for homeowners, and biosolids management. While the company serves individual households, businesses, municipalities, the U.S. military, and industrial entities, residential customers comprise the vast majority of its clientele in regulated activities. The company operates primarily through its Regulated Businesses segment, which owns subsidiaries providing drinking water, wastewater, and related services to residential, commercial, industrial, and public authority customers across approximately 1,600 communities in the United States and Canada. The company also manages four non-reportable market-based businesses offering complementary water and wastewater services. Its Regulated Businesses generally own the physical assets for storing, pumping, treating, and delivering water, as well as collecting, treating, and recycling wastewater. Customers include individuals, corporations, municipalities, and government entities, with residential customers comprising the majority of the base. The company serves these customers through distribution systems, supplying water for domestic use, commercial operations, industrial processes, firefighting, and bulk distribution to other utilities. American Water Works operates two primary business categories: Regulated Businesses and Market-Based Businesses. The Regulated Businesses provide water and wastewater services to municipalities and other local government entities, operating under state public utility commissions. The Market-Based Businesses serve a diverse client base including military bases, homeowners, smaller commercial customers, municipalities, the food and beverage industry, and natural gas exploration and production companies. Specifically, the Military Services Group manages water and wastewater systems on U.S. military bases; the Homeowner Services Group offers warranty-type repairs for plumbing and electrical lines to residential and small commercial customers; the Contract Operations Group provides operations and maintenance services for municipal and industrial facilities; and the Keystone segment delivers customized water sourcing, transfer, and pipeline construction services to energy companies.
